Pinto Sd/- =============================================================== Approved for Reporting = ============================================================== State Of Gujarat Thro D Y Yaduvanshi, Food Inspector Versus Dalpatsinh Udesinh Rathod & Anr. =============================================================== Appearance: Ms Cm Shah, App for the Appellant(s) No. 1 Rule Served for the Opponent(s)/Respondent(s) No. 1 Unserved Expired (R) for the Opponent(s)/Respondent(s) No. 2 ====== == == == == ========================= = Coram:Honourable Ms. Justice S.V. Pinto Date : 18/07/2025
texts.facts: 1 2. This appeal has been filed by the appellant - State under Section 378(1)(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/285/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 18/07/2025 undefined (hereinafter referred to as 'the Code') against the impugned judgment and the order passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate, First Class, Savli (hereinafter referred to as 'the learned Trial Court') in Criminal Case No.492 of 1994 on 19.03.2012, whereby, the learned Trial Court has acquitted the respondent - accused from the offences punishable under Sections 7(1) and 16(1)(a)(1) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act'). 1.1. The respondents hereinafter referred to as 'the accused' as they stood in the rank and file in the original case, for the sake of convenience, clarity and brevity. 2. The relevant facts leading to filing of the present appeal are as under: 2.1. The complainant - Devendrapalsinh Yagnapalsinh Yaduvanshi was a notified Food Inspector and on 17.04.1993, along with helper B.L.Parmar visited the shop of the accused no.1 at Poicha, Taluka Savli and the accused no.1 was present in the shop. The accused no. 1 was a grocer and there was a 15kg packed NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/285/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 18/07/2025 undefined tin of groundnut oil, on which, a label of 'Girnar' Pure Groundnut Oil Mmnufactured by "Balmukund Industries, Sabalpur, Junagadh" was affixed. The packed tin was for human consumption and from the packed tin, 500 grams of groundnut oil was purchased after the entire procedure was followed, the 500 grams of groundnut oil was placed in equal proportions in three clean and dry glass jars and after the jars were sealed and labelled, they were placed in brown paper and sealed and one sample was sent to the Public Analyst as per the procedure and the other two samples were sent to the Local Health Authority. The report of the Public Analyst was received, which showed that the sample did not conform to the standards and provisions laid down under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955, and after the permission for filing the complaint was received, the complaint was filed by the complainant Devendrapalsinh Yagnapalsinh Yaduvanshi against the accused no. 1, who was the vendor, the accused no. 2, who was the warrantor and the accused no. 3, who was the producer. 2.2. During the trial before the learned Trial Court, the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/285/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 18/07/2025 undefined accused no. 3, who was the producer, could not be traced out and the complainant could not produce the new address of the accused no. 3 and non-bailable warrants were sent, but they could not be served, and hence, the accused no. 3 was deleted from the case. 2.3. The accused was duly served with the summons and the accused appeared before the learned Trial Court and it was verified whether the copies of all the papers were provided to the accused as per the provisions of Section 207 of the Code. As the case was a private warrant triable case, the evidence of the complainant on oath was recorded. Considering the evidence on record, as prima-facie case was made out, a charge was framed by the learned Trial Court at Exh.112 and the statements of the accused were recorded at Exhs.113 and 114, wherein, the accused denied all the State Of Gujarat Thro D Y Yaduvanshi, ... vs Dalpatsinh Udesinh Rathod on 18 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191281490/ 2 contents of the charge and the further evidence of the prosecution was taken on record. As the original accused No.3 was not available, the learned Trial Court has deleted the accused no. 3 from the case and the trial was proceeded against the respondent nos. 1 and 2. The prosecution examined 2 witnesses i.e. the complainant - Devendrapalsinh Yagnapalsinh Yaduvanshi at NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/285/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 18/07/2025 undefined Exh.70 and PW-2 Jagdishprasad Mukundlal Shah at Exh.117 and has produced 36 documentary evidences in support of the case. 2.4. After the evidence of the complainant was closed, the further statement of the accused under Section 313 of the Code were recorded wherein in the accused denied the evidence on record. 3. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and order passed by the learned Trial Court, the appellant - State has filed the present appeal mainly stating that the impugned judgment and order of acquittal passed by the learned Trial Court is contrary to law, evidence on record and principles of natural justice.
texts.arguments: Learned APP Ms.C.M.Shah for the appellant - State has taken this Court through the entire evidence produced by the prosecution and has vehemently argued that the learned Trial Court has not appreciated the evidence properly and the prosecution has produced cogent evidence to prove the case and has successfully proved the case against the accused but the learned Trial Court has not considered the same and has acquitted the accused. The judgment and order of acquittal passed by the learned Judge is contrary to law, evidence on record and principles of justice. Learned APP has urged this Court to quash and [LEAKAGE_MASK] the impugned judgment and order of acquittal and to find the accused guilty for the said offence and impose maximum sentence on the accused. 6. At the outset, before discussing the facts of the present case, it would be appropriate to refer to the observations of the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/285/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 18/07/2025 undefined Apex Court in the case of Chandrappa & Ors. Vs. State of Karnataka reported in 2007 (4) SCC 415, the Apex Court has observed as under: Recently, in Kallu Vs. State of M.P. (2006) 10 SCC 313 : AIR 2006 SC 831, this Court stated; "While deciding an appeal against acquittal, the power of the Appellate Court is no less than the power exercised while hearing appeals against conviction. In both types of appeals, the power exists to review the entire evidence. However, one significant difference is that an order of acquittal will not be interfered with, by an appellate court, where the judgment of the trial court is based on evidence and the view taken is reasonable and plausible. ........
